thread:
evan: Heads-up — noticed traffic going to svc-b even when host is *.example.com and we have an explicit host exception for beta.example.com. Behavior looks like wildcard is winning. Anyone seen this?

yasmin: yep saw it in canary. logs look like `matched wildcard-host rule` before explicit host. Minimal repro is a curl with Host set to beta.example.com.

evans: repro steps and config below — maybe I'm missing something in matcher rules.

kevin: that's definitely wrong. Exact host matches should always outrank a wildcard. We need a deterministic precedence: exact literal > wildcard with fewer wildcards > catch-all. Path specificity should apply after host resolution.

sophia: quick note: our sorter currently uses a token-count heuristic that treats `*` as a token with same weight as literals. That would make `*.example.com` tie with `beta.example.com` in some cases. Could be the bug.

evans: Reproducer + config snippet:
```yaml
- host: "*.example.com"
  service: svc-b
  path: "/"
- host: "beta.example.com"
  service: svc-a
  path: "/"
```
Curl: `curl -H "Host: beta.example.com" https://gateway/internal-route` -> svc-b response.

kevin: Proposed simple scoring: exact match gets a big constant boost. Example pseudocode:
```
host_score = 0
if host_pattern == request_host: host_score += 10000
host_score += literal_char_count(host_pattern) - wildcard_count(host_pattern)*50
// total_score = host_score * 1000 + path_score(...)
```
This keeps exact matches first, and otherwise prefers more literal content and fewer wildcards.

yasmin: I like the simple constant boost. Less risky than a whole new grammar. We should also add an integration test matrix for host/path combos. I'll take tests.

sophia: two gotchas: 1) header overrides (X-Host-Override) — we currently validate it but then pass it through; precedence logic needs to treat it as the canonical host if present. 2) negative exceptions (e.g. exclude malicious.example.com) — we don't support that syntax. Do we want to add `!` or a separate `except_hosts` field? That feels larger.

evans: For immediate fix: implement exact-match boost + ensure header override host uses the same scoring pipeline. Create an RFC for negative exceptions and `except_hosts` — sounds useful for tenants that want a global wildcard but blacklist some subdomains. I'll draft the RFC.

kevin: I'll put up a small patch to change scoring in matcher.go and add unit tests. Branch: `fix/host-precedence-1999`.

yasmin: I'll add an integration test in `gateway/testcases/host_precedence_test.go` covering: exact literal vs wildcard, wildcard vs catch-all, header-override behaviour.

sophia: also add a fuzz test for host patterns with many dots/wildcards so we don't regress on perf.

deploy-bot: ci/presubmit for fix/host-precedence-1999 started.

yasmin: CI green on unit tests. :white_check_mark:

kevin: PR up: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/986 — small change to scoring + docs update in route-matching.md

evans: reviewed, left one nit on a comment. overall LGTM.

yasmin: merging now. :shipit: 

sophia: + follow-up: evan create RFC issue for `except_hosts` and include example grammar and expected precedence semantics. I'll comment on design.

evans: filing RFC: https://go/redwood/rfc/host-exceptions-1999 — draft created.

deploy-bot: presubmit passed and merged into `main` (CI build 4821) :white_check_mark:

kevin: rolling a canary — watching metrics for misroutes.

yasmin: saw the canary hit svc-a for beta.example.com, good. Will keep an eye on alpha and wildcard corners.

evans: thanks all. We'll follow up in the RFC thread for grammar changes.
